definition: An umbrella term for practices and principles aimed at ensuring AI systems are developed and used ethically, safely, and beneficially.
details: Responsible AI encompasses fairness, transparency, privacy, safety, and accountability considerations throughout the AI development lifecycle, from data collection through deployment and monitoring.

explainer.lead: Responsible AI is an umbrella term for practices and principles aimed at making AI systems ethical, safe, and beneficial. It matters because these concerns span the whole lifecycle, from data collection to deployment and monitoring.

tiers.eli5: It is the set of house rules for building and running AI: be fair, be open, protect privacy, stay safe, and own your mistakes.
tiers.practitioner: Teams apply it across the development lifecycle, covering fairness, transparency, privacy, safety, and accountability. A pitfall is treating it as a one-time checklist rather than ongoing monitoring after deployment.
tiers.paperLevel: An umbrella term for practices and principles ensuring AI systems are developed and used ethically, safely, and beneficially, spanning fairness, transparency, privacy, safety, and accountability throughout the lifecycle. It names no single metric or standard.

explainer.example: A team documents data provenance at collection, tests for bias before release, and monitors deployed models for harmful behaviour.
